# Draw what happens inside a payment-gateway request

*Acme Retail · October 2026 · generated by ddreview 1.0.0 · facts.json 3827d58e72d8*

Draw a Mermaid `flowchart LR`: a request node, then the application node (`Java servlet`), then one node per child kind with the per-request ratio on the edge label (for example `~25 statements per request`). Style amber any kind above these thresholds: database 10, HTTP 5, cache 10, secret-store reads 0.1 per request. The notebook already says above the diagram that these are sample ratios (in the 9-minute sample).

| Child kind | Per request (sample ratio) |
|---|---|
| db | 0.25 |
| http | 0.27 |

Mermaid rules (Datadog's renderer is conservative):
- Start with `flowchart TB` or `flowchart LR`; put every label in double quotes; use `<br/>` for a line break inside a label.
- Node ids start with an upper-case letter and are 2-40 letters, digits or underscores (for example `Svc_checkout`, `Db_orders`), never `End`; real names go in the quoted label.
- Every `subgraph Id["title"]` has its own `direction LR` (or TB) line straight after it, and closes with `end`.
- Shapes: `Svc_a["service"]`, `Db_b[("database")]`, `Host_c(["external host"])`. Edges: `Svc_a -->|"label"| Db_b`. Styles: `style Svc_a fill:#ffe0e0,stroke:#c62828,color:#000` (red) or `fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#b8860b,color:#000` (amber).
- One statement per line: declare every node on its own line before any edge or style that uses it; one edge per line with spaces around the arrow; no chained edges, no `&`, no semicolons.
- At most 20 nodes and 40 edges. No classDef, no frontmatter, no markdown inside labels, no xychart/timeline/mindmap.
- Output only the Mermaid code in one ```mermaid fence, nothing else.

---
After pasting the diagram into the notebook, validate the notebook: `python -m ddreview validate <notebook.md> --facts facts.json` (it lints every Mermaid block).
`validate --against` compares the numbers of each section with the original notebook: a number added or changed is an error, a number dropped is a warning. `validate --text` alone only rejects a figure that facts.json cannot produce in any format, so a typo that happens to match another fact passes. Neither checks a value inside a Mermaid block: read the diagram against the tables before pasting it.
